MDBA gauge getter uses datasource = 'CP' for NSW, 'PUBLISH' for QLD, and 'AT' for Vic. I just used 'A' for flow scaling, and don't see a reason to change unless there are issues.

Some of the gauges come in multiple times if they hit multiple planning units. But we don't need to pull them multiple times, so finish off with a `unique`.

Extraction and check functions

```{r}
extract_safely <- function(safelist) {
  
  safelist <- purrr::list_transpose(safelist, simplify = FALSE)
  
  # Some checks
  errornums <- which(purrr::map_lgl(safelist$error, \(x) !is.null(x)))

  rlang::inform(glue::glue("There were {length(errornums)} errors."))
  
  return(safelist)
}

check_dataframe_list <- function(dflist) {
  datarows <- purrr::map_int(dflist, 
                           \(x) if (is.null(x)) {0} else {nrow(x)})
  
  # Not sure these informs are useful, since it'll depend on what we're trying to do.
    datazero <- length(which(datarows == 0))

  # These are the ones to watch out for that will be doubled
  datamulti <- length(which(datarows > 1))
  rlang::inform(c(glue::glue("There were {datazero} 0-row dfs and {datamulti} with more than 1 row.")))
  return(datarows)
}
```

```{r}
state_table <- ewr_gauges |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  filter(!grepl('SA - Department', owner)) |> 
  mutate(var_list = case_when(gaugetype == 'F' ~ 141,
                              gaugetype == 'L' ~ 100,
                              gaugetype == 'LL' ~ 130),
         portal = stringr::str_extract(owner, 'VIC|NSW|QLD') |> stringr::str_to_lower(),
         start_time = 'all',
         end_time = 'all',
         timeunit = 'day',
         statistic = 'mean',
         datasource = 'A',
         request_timezone = 'db_default',
         return_timezone = 'UTC') |> 
  select(portal, gauge, var_list, start_time, end_time, 
         timeunit, statistic, datasource, request_timezone, return_timezone) |> 
  filter(!is.na(portal)) |> # Remove unassigned gauges with no way to pull 
  unique()

bom_table <- ewr_gauges |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  filter(grepl('SA - Department', owner)) |> 
  mutate(portal = 'bom',
         start_time = 'all',
         end_time = 'all',
         # this will need to be checked carefully
         variable = case_when(gaugetype == 'F' ~ 'discharge',
                              gaugetype == 'L' ~ 'level',
                              gaugetype == 'LL' ~ 'Reservoir Water Level AHD'),
         units = case_when(gaugetype == 'F' ~ 'cumec',
                              gaugetype == 'L' ~ 'm', # is this unique?
                              gaugetype == 'LL' ~ 'm AHD'),
         timeunit = 'Daily',
         statistic = 'Mean',
         datatype = 'QaQc.*24',
         request_timezone = 'db_default',
         return_timezone = 'UTC') |> 
  select(portal, gauge, variable, units, start_time, end_time, 
         timeunit, statistic, datatype, request_timezone, return_timezone) |> 
  unique()


```

Standardize the naming

```{r}
bomrename <- function(bomdata) {

  bomdata |>
        dplyr::rename(gauge = station_no,
                      name = station_name,
                      variable_name = parametertype_name,
                      units = ts_unitsymbol) |>
        dplyr::mutate(source = 'bom') |>
        dplyr::select(gauge, name, variable_name, 
                      units, value, quality_code, 
                      time, database_timezone, source)
}

staterename <- function(statedata) {
  statedata |>
        dplyr::select(-variable_name) |>
        dplyr::rename(gauge = site,
                      name = site_name,
                      quality_code = quality_codes_id) |>
        dplyr::mutate(variable_name = stringr::str_remove_all(variable_short_name, ' \\(.*'),
                      units = stringr::str_remove_all(variable_short_name, '.*\\(|\\)'),
                      source = 'state') |> # Would be good to use the portal name, but we'd need to retain it
        dplyr::select(-variable_short_name) |>
        dplyr::select(gauge, name, variable_name, units, value, quality_code, time, database_timezone, source)
}
```

```{r}
# set those up into checker functions
onerowperday <- function(x) {
  tdiff <- x$time[length(x$time)] - x$time[1]
  tdiff == nrow(x)-1
}

nomissing <- function(x) {
  tdiffs <- x$time - lag(x$time)
  return(max(tdiffs, na.rm = TRUE) == 1)
}

# this in particular woudl be easy to use as \(x)
duptimes <- function(x) {
  any(duplicated(x$time))
}
```

Make a summary for data availability

```{r}
summarise_gauges <- function(x) {
  if (all(!grepl('ml/d', x$units, ignore.case = TRUE))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  x |> 
    filter(grepl('ml/d', units, ignore.case = TRUE)) |> 
    summarise(gauge = unique(gauge), 
              name = unique(name),
              start = min(time),
              end = max(time),
              proportion_bad = sum(quality_code > 150, na.rm = TRUE)/n())
}

```


### Make EWR

```{r}
make_ewrformat <- function(x) {
  x <- x |> 
    dplyr::mutate(gauge = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl('ml/d', units, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ paste0(gauge, '_flow'),
      units %in% c('m', 'Res. Level AHD', 'Metres') ~ paste0(gauge, '_level'),
      .default = paste0(gauge, '_FAIL'))
      ) |> 
    dplyr::select(Date = time, gauge, value) |> 
    tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = Date, names_from = gauge, values_from = value) |> 
    dplyr::mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))
  return(x)
}
```

```{r}

state_simple <- purrr::map(state_ts2, make_ewrformat)
```

First, we need the range of dates

```{r}
alldates <- purrr::map(both_simple,
                       \(x) dplyr::select(x, Date)) |> 
  purrr::list_rbind() |> 
  dplyr::distinct(Date) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(Date)
```

Then we need to go through each table and `left_join` them on by `Date` . I think `reduce` is the `purrr` way to avoid for loops or foreach (`accumulate`) gives the intermediate steps too.)

```{r}
all_results <- both_simple |> 
  purrr::reduce(.f = \(x, y) dplyr::left_join(x, y, by = 'Date'),
                    .init = alldates)
```

```{r}
                      filter(grepl('discharge', parametertype_name, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
                        filter(grepl('DailyMean', ts_name, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>

                      unique()) |> 
  purrr::list_rbind()

bommiss
```

Let's look at the ewr table

```{r}
#| eval: false
et <- get_ewr_table()

etcumec <- et |> 
  filter(Gauge %in% c(bom_table$gauge[2:5]))
```

What's going on with 6 and 7? They don't break on the 09. *Should we just change them to 24? Should we change everything to 24*? mdba_gauge_getter gets the flows at 09, but the levels (and LL) at 24. Why? I don't really see a reason not to use the 24 everywhere.

```{r}
#| eval: false
boml2[6:7] |> purrr::map(\(x) x |>  
                           filter(grepl('level', parametertype_name, ignore.case = TRUE) & 
                                    grepl('mean', ts_name, ignore.case = TRUE) &
                                    grepl('daily', ts_name, ignore.case = TRUE)) |> 
                      select(station_no, ts_name, ts_unitsymbol) |> 
                      unique()) |> 
  purrr::list_rbind()
```
